subject: Chemistry
title: β-Elimination and Saytzeff Rule: Which Alkene Wins?
summary: Heating an alkyl halide with alcoholic KOH removes the halogen and a hydrogen from the next carbon: an alkene forms. In this lesson: alcoholic KOH and heat, dehydrohalogenation of bromoethane, α- and β-carbons, the bond changes with curved arrows (base takes the β-H, C=C forms, Br- leaves), 2-bromopentane giving pent-2-ene (81 %) and pent-1-ene (19 %), the Saytzeff rule, and two solved questions.

notes.title: β-Elimination and Saytzeff Rule
notes.blurb: the reaction, what happens (bond changes), saytzeff (zaitsev) rule, solved questions

keyPoints: **β-Elimination**: **Alcoholic KOH, heat**: H and X leave. Also called **dehydrohalogenation**.
**α and β**: α carries the **halogen**. β is the **next** carbon.
**In one go**: Three curved arrows, **one step**. Products: alkene, **H₂O, Br⁻**.

blocks.p: This is **dehydrohalogenation** (removal of HX). The carbon bearing the halogen is the **α-carbon**; the carbon next to it is the **β-carbon**. The hydrogen always leaves from a β-carbon: **β-elimination**.

list: ① The base (OH⁻) removes a β-hydrogen as H⁺ (forming H₂O).
② The electron pair of the C–H bond moves between Cα and Cβ to form the π bond (C=C).
③ The C–Br bond breaks; its electron pair leaves with Br⁻.
In this picture all three changes happen together, in one step.

blocks.p: When there are two or more kinds of β-hydrogen, more than one alkene can form. The **major product is the more substituted alkene**: the one with more alkyl groups on the doubly bonded carbons. It is the more stable alkene.

list: ✗ The hydrogen leaves from the α-carbon (it leaves from a β-carbon).
✗ The less substituted alkene is major (by Saytzeff, the more substituted one is).
✗ Aqueous KOH gives the alkene (aqueous KOH mainly substitutes to give the alcohol; alcoholic KOH eliminates).

blocks.p: **Q1.** 2-Bromobutane + alc. KOH, heat → but-2-ene (major, 2 alkyl groups) and but-1-ene (minor).
**Q2.** 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane → 2-methylbut-2-ene (major, 3 alkyl groups on C=C) rather than 2-methylbut-1-ene (2).

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: The one giving maximum number of isomeric alkenes on dehydrohalogenation reaction is (excluding rearrangement):
pyq.explain: 2-Bromopentane gives pent-1-ene, cis-pent-2-ene and trans-pent-2-ene: 3. 1-Bromo-2-methylbutane: one (2-methylbut-1-ene). 2-Bromopropane: propene only. 2-Bromo-3,3-dimethylpentane: C3 has no H, so only 3,3-dimethylpent-1-ene.
